contexts.text: Spirits and Angels speak to man in his vernacular. Explained. DLW 257:2. DP 135. CL 326:4. SE 2137. SE 2309. SE 2608. SE 5770.
From (the spiritual language) ideas inflow into my vernacular, and so they speak.
I said to the Angels that perhaps they suppose they speak to me in my vernacular, because it is so apperceived...
So with man's speech the sense falls into the words without the man thinking about it.
In the other life (these) speak the spiritual language, but mixed with their vernacular language, so that it can be plainly seen from what nation they are.
(The exhortation before the Holy Supper) shall be quoted in the vernacular in which it is written. (It follows, in English.)
